ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Benny Leonard Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care at 50 after a referee's license examination found high blood pressure: exertional breathlessness and chest tightness while refereeing, an ECG showing left ventricular hypertrophy, cardiovascular risk, money worries and mood, and a cardiology consultation. Concerns: Breathless and tight in the chest late in long nights in the ring, and told his blood pressure is high; He needs his refereeing work and is afraid of losing his license; Worry about money since losing his savings years ago, and about the cost of medicines. [S]

tr.td: Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 78 per minute; left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage (Sokolow-Lyon 38 mm, Cornell 24 mm) with mild lateral T-wave flattening; PR 160 ms; QRS 96 ms; QTc 418 ms; no Q waves, pre-excitation, conduction block or Brugada pattern

Transthoracic echocardiogram: concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum 13 mm, posterior wall 12 mm, septal-to-posterior ratio 1.1, mass index 118 g/m2); ejection fraction 62% without regional wall motion abnormality; grade 1 diastolic dysfunction; left atrial volume index 36 mL/m2; no systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve or outflow tract obstruction at rest or with Valsalva; normal valves; aortic root 34 mm

Exercise stress echocardiogram (Bruce protocol): 9 minutes 30 seconds, about 10.5 METs; peak heart rate 156 per minute (92% of predicted); blood pressure 150/92 at rest rising to 226/98 mmHg at peak, an exaggerated response; mild breathlessness at peak without chest discomfort; no ST-segment change; no arrhythmia; normal augmentation of all wall segments, with no inducible ischemia

Noncontrast CT of the heart for coronary calcium: Agatston score 186 (left anterior descending 118, right coronary 52, circumflex 16), about the 80th percentile for his age and sex; no other cardiac finding
Resting 12-lead ECG at the sick visit: sinus tachycardia at 104 per minute; left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage, unchanged; QTc 432 ms; no ischemic change or arrhythmia
Advance care planning conversation, about 15 minutes, with his consent

list.item: Breathlessness and tightness across the chest on exertion for about two months, late in long nights of refereeing in hot arenas, easing within a few minutes of rest; never at rest; no fainting, palpitations, orthopnea or ankle swelling; cause under evaluation with a cardiology consultation: resolved, confirmed [S]

Stage 2 hypertension found at a yearly fitness examination for his referee's license (164/100 and 160/98 mmHg), with left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage on the ECG; untreated; home readings to follow: resolved, confirmed [S]

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum 13 mm, mass index 118 g/m2) with normal ejection fraction, grade 1 diastolic dysfunction, a mildly enlarged left atrium and an exaggerated blood pressure rise on exercise; no features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: active, confirmed [S]

Coronary atherosclerosis found by coronary calcium scoring (Agatston score 186, about the 80th percentile for his age and sex), without angina and with no inducible ischemia on exercise stress echocardiography: active, confirmed [S]
Hypercholesterolemia: LDL 160 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, lipoprotein(a) not raised; no diabetes: active, confirmed [S]

Volume depletion after refereeing a long card in a heat wave while taking losartan 100 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg: lightheaded on standing, with an orthostatic fall in blood pressure, a prerenal rise in creatinine to 1.44 mg/dL and potassium 3.3 mmol/L; no fainting, chest pain or arrhythmia: resolved, confirmed [S]

list.item: Referee of professional boxing several nights a week, usually working a whole card of six to eight bouts, and a boxing instructor at a city college; a former world lightweight champion who served in the merchant marine in wartime [S]

Lost most of his savings in a market crash years ago and went back to fighting to rebuild them; money is steady now but tight; worries that a failed license examination would cost him his refereeing work; asked for low-cost medicines [S]
Jewish; raised in an Orthodox family on the Lower East Side; keeps the major holidays, and asked that visits not be booked on them [S]
Never smoked; a glass of wine on the Sabbath and holidays (AUDIT-C 2); no drug use [S]

Walks a great deal and moves constantly in the ring on fight nights, but does no other regular exercise since he stopped training; eats late after fights, often salted deli meats, pickles and soup [S]
Strengths: quick, disciplined and well informed; a respected figure in boxing with many friends; steady work; wants to keep refereeing and teaching [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care at 50 after a referee's license examination found high blood pressure: exertional breathlessness and chest tightness while refereeing, an ECG showing left ventricular hypertrophy, cardiovascular risk, money worries and mood, and a cardiology consultation
Two-week review on the day of the cardiology consultation: the echocardiogram, stress test and calcium score, home blood pressure, a statin, and refereeing
Seven-week review: home blood pressure, the first weeks back at full cards, symptoms, and a dose increase
Fifteen-week review: blood pressure after the change of medicine, kidney function and potassium, cholesterol on the statin, and the sick visit
Twenty-four-week review: blood pressure control, symptoms at work, mood and worry, aspirin, and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for lightheadedness after refereeing in the heat
Periodic adult preventive visit and recheck after the sick visit

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: High blood pressure: home monitoring with a validated upper-arm cuff, twice a day, with readings sent in weekly; single-pill losartan 50 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg from today, chosen as two first-line drugs for stage 2 hypertension and a low-cost generic; basic metabolic panel in two weeks; target below 130/80 mmHg; less salt (no more than 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day), the DASH pattern, and regular walking

Cardiology consultation for exertional breathlessness and chest tightness with left ventricular hypertrophy on the ECG: the cause, the type of hypertrophy, sudden cardiac death risk, coronary risk testing, and whether he can keep refereeing

Evaluation at intake: resting ECG, basic metabolic panel, TSH, HbA1c, lipid panel, one-time lipoprotein(a) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; stop and rest, and call the same day for chest discomfort at rest or lasting more than a few minutes, fainting or palpitations; referee only short undercards until the consultation

Atorvastatin 40 mg each evening after a coronary calcium score of 186, aiming for LDL below 70 mg/dL and at least a 50% fall, with a lipid panel at eight to twelve weeks; aspirin discussed and not started while blood pressure is uncontrolled, to be revisited

Return to work: short undercards until home blood pressure is below 140/90 mmHg, then full cards; drink water between bouts in hot arenas; stop and hand over the bout for chest discomfort, faintness or palpitations; hold the blood pressure tablet on sick days (vomiting, diarrhea, or unable to drink) and call; the venue to keep a defibrillator at ringside with staff trained in CPR; repeat echocardiogram in six to twelve months
Losartan 100 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg each morning; basic metabolic panel two weeks after the increase
Volume depletion: oral fluids with salt and potassium-rich foods; hold losartan-hydrochlorothiazide until the recheck in one week; no refereeing until then; emergency care for fainting or chest pain

Change to losartan 100 mg and amlodipine 5 mg each morning, without the thiazide, because of heavy sweating in hot arenas; basic metabolic panel in four weeks; written sick-day rules on a card for his wallet
Money worries and mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at six months; generic once-daily medicines at the lowest cost; a social needs screen; brief support and problem-solving at each visit
